conceptZh: 科學家老鼠的燒杯太滿，泡泡推倒一串試管，倒成「太」，最後一滴冒出一顆小太陽。
object: a bespectacled cartoon lab mouse, a rack of test tubes filled with orange liquid, and an overflowing beaker with a tiny cartoon sun inside
morph: a row of tumbling orange test tubes lands in the strokes of the glyph 太 and a tiny sun rises from the overflowing beaker
creativeAngle: 骨牌效應：燒杯「太滿」溢出，推倒試管骨牌倒成「太」，最後一點正好是燒杯滴出的小點；詞「太陽」用小太陽升起呼應。
promptEn: An 8-second whimsical lab clip on a clean solid pale seafoam backdrop. The only text in frame is one large Traditional Chinese glyph 太, formed by glossy saturated orange test tubes lying flat as thick strokes plus a single round drop as the final dot, about 70% of frame height, centered with margins. Lead: a bespectacled cartoon lab mouse in a tiny white coat among bubbling beakers that fizz over on cue; one supporting object, a beaker too full of orange liquid. No background music, no subtitles, no vocabulary text. Voice: warm, friendly off-screen narrator in clear Taiwanese Mandarin saying exactly 太、太、太陽 (ㄊㄞˋ、ㄊㄞˋ、ㄊㄞˋ ㄧㄤˊ), slow clear tones, then silence. Moment 1 (0–1.6s): the mouse pours orange liquid into a beaker that is already full; as the first 太 is spoken, the liquid rises, balloons over the rim in a dome, and the mouse's eyes grow huge behind his glasses. Moment 2 (1.6–3.2s): a wobbling bubble pops off the beaker and bonks the first of a long row of standing test tubes; the tubes tip one by one with soft clinks, and the mouse scurries along them, trying to stop the chain with his tail and clipboard, tangling himself in his own lab coat. Moment 3 (3.2–5s): the tubes roll to a stop as the second 太 is spoken, landing exactly into the glyph 太: a long horizontal bar, a sweeping left falling stroke, a right falling stroke, and below the crossing, a single round dot. The mouse pops out, sees it, and flips his glasses up with a hop. Moment 4 (5s): as 太陽 is spoken, the last drop falls from the beaker onto the dot position, and a tiny round cartoon sun with a smiling face rises from the beaker, spinning small rays, bobbing at the mouse's nose. Final 5–8s: the glyph 太 stays absolutely still and legible while the mouse and the little sun hold hands and dance a small shuffle near the lower edge, the sun bobbing up and down, never touching the strokes. Soft daylight, no flashing (the sun glows steadily, no pulses), no real people, no other text.

conceptZh: 玩具戰士踮腳偷拿浣熊花生頂著的大橘球，球太大抱不動，撞醒花生，兩人面對面大叫，一陣亂轉把三根泡棉棒和球摔成「太」，最後舉起笑臉太陽盾牌。
object: three long orange foam bars stacked on a dozing raccoon guard, with one big round orange ball balanced on top
morph: the sneak-and-surprise collision flings the three bars down as the horizontal, left-falling and right-falling strokes of 太, and the ball drops into the slot below the crossing as the final dot
creativeAngle: 全新「偷襲被抓包」實體笑料：戰士想要的東西「太大」了，正好呼應字義；碰撞本身把道具摔成筆畫，不再是試管骨牌或拉炮；結尾用戰士的圓盾翻出笑臉太陽，讓「太陽」一詞有畫面可對。
promptEn: An 8-second slapstick toy clip on a clean solid pale butter-cream backdrop with soft even daylight, nothing behind the characters. The only text in frame is one large Traditional Chinese glyph 太, built from three long glossy saturated orange-red foam bars plus one round orange ball as the dot; when finished it fills about 70% of frame height, centered with margins, never cropped. Lead: a chunky toy warrior figure with a round shield and a floppy foam sword, all bravado and no skill, who swings so hard he spins himself around. One supporting character: Peanut, a cartoon raccoon in a tiny guard helmet, dozing on a stool at center-right while balancing a wobbling stack of three long orange foam bars with a big orange ball on top. No background music, no subtitles, no vocabulary text. Voice: a warm, friendly off-screen narrator in clear Taiwanese Mandarin says exactly 太、太、太陽 (ㄊㄞˋ、ㄊㄞˋ、ㄊㄞˋ ㄧㄤˊ), reading exactly those syllables slowly with clear tones, then silence. Moment 1, want it (0 to 1.5s): the warrior pops in at the lower-left, spots the ball on top of Peanut's stack, points at it with his sword, rubs his hands, and raises one knee high for a tiptoe. Peanut snores little bubbles. Moment 2, the sneak (1.5 to 3.2s): as the first 太 is spoken, the warrior tiptoes across the frame left to right with huge exaggerated high steps; each step makes a small squeak and Peanut's ear flicks, Peanut's stack tilts, the warrior freezes mid-step on one foot, then creeps on. Moment 3, the surprise and crash (3.2 to 5.2s): the warrior stretches up and hugs the ball, but it is far too big for him; he staggers backward and bonks Peanut on the nose with his sword tip. Peanut's eyes snap open, the two are nose to nose, both open their mouths in a wide silent cartoon yell with a soft boing, and Peanut salutes so hard the stack launches. The warrior swings his foam sword in panic, spins like a top, and the second 太 is spoken as the three bars thump down one, two, three into the glyph 太: a long horizontal bar, a sweeping left-falling bar, a right-falling bar crossing it, and the ball drops with a plop into the dot slot just below the crossing. Moment 4, the payoff (5.2 to 8s): the glyph 太 stays perfectly still and readable. At about 6s, as 太陽 is spoken, the dizzy warrior sits up at the lower-left corner and raises his round shield over his head like a sunrise; the shield face is painted as a smiling cartoon sun with short rays, glowing steadily. Peanut, at the lower-right, snaps a proud salute to the shield a beat too late, then wobbles. Neither touches or covers the strokes. Cartoon squash-and-stretch, bright warm colors, no neon, no flashing, no real people, no other text.
